quality_guards: Gas-safety controls depend on appliance type, fuel, installation, ventilation, flue condition, maintenance history, occupancy and competent-person findings.
Gas-safety evidence is appliance-, premises- and condition-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fire, explosion or poisoning probability.
LPG controls depend on fuel quantity, storage type, tank or cylinder condition, ventilation, separation, vehicle impact, pipework, ignition sources and emergency arrangements.
LPG evidence is installation-, inventory- and site-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fire or explosion probability.
Lead controls depend on lead form, process, dust or fume generation, airborne and biological monitoring, worker age or health, hygiene and control performance.
Lead evidence is substance-, task-, exposure- and worker-specific and is not an exact parcel-level illness probability.
Ionising-radiation controls depend on source type, activity or energy, shielding, distance, time, work classification, dose assessment, occupancy and emergency scenarios.
Ionising-radiation evidence is source-, practice-, worker- and site-specific and is not an exact parcel-level dose or health probability.
Biological-agent controls depend on agent classification, transmission route, concentration, activity, containment, worker susceptibility, environmental survival and emergency arrangements.
Biological-agent evidence is agent-, activity-, workplace- and person-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection probability.
Sharps controls depend on device, procedure, patient or material contamination, user competence, disposal route, staffing, environment and post-exposure response.
Sharps evidence is device-, task-, exposure- and worker-specific and is not an exact parcel-level infection or injury probability.
Workplace-transport controls depend on site layout, traffic volume, vehicle type, pedestrian flows, visibility, reversing, surfaces, loading activity, driver competence and maintenance.
Workplace-transport evidence is site-, vehicle-, task- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level collision probability.
Motor-repair controls depend on vehicle technology, repair task, lifting method, tyre or pressure system, paint or chemical, hot work, workshop layout and worker competence.
Motor-vehicle-repair evidence is vehicle-, task-, workshop- and worker-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury or illness probability.
Warehouse controls depend on goods, racking, stacking height, lift trucks, loading bays, pedestrian flows, shift patterns, temperature, fire load and emergency arrangements.
Warehousing evidence is facility-, inventory-, operation- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury or fire probability.
Maintenance controls depend on equipment, energy sources, failure mode, access, isolation points, stored energy, contractor interfaces, production state and worker competence.
Maintenance evidence is equipment-, task-, energy- and site-specific and is not an exact parcel-level injury probability.
Official-source context is not converted into an exact parcel-level probability.
